steps.name: Sciurus
steps.text: Tch. It's taking too long.

steps.name: Ratatos
steps.text: Keep it down, Sciurus. You're interrupting my train of thought.

steps.name: Sciurus
steps.text: What's to think about? Enciodes has to hand his land over this time.

steps.name: Ratatos
steps.text: Yucatan, your opinion?

steps.name: Yucatan
steps.text: ...I agree with Rus, but Sir Enciodes won't just lie down and take it.

steps.name: Ratatos
steps.text: At least you think before you talk. Unlike your wife here.

steps.name: Sciurus
steps.text: Oh, who exactly is this about?!

steps.name: Ratatos
steps.text: You, of course, my beautiful little sister.

steps.name: Ratatos
steps.text: If only it wasn't for Arctosz and his idiot face firing off at anything to do with Karlan. I didn't want to fall out with Enciodes this soon, that's for sure.

steps.name: Ratatos
steps.text: People like Enciodes are a handful. Even if he croaks, he'll be sure to put us on the brink too at least. Not to mention...

steps.name: Ratatos
steps.text: Something tells me he won't accept his sorry lot, and it's telling me loud.

steps.name: Sciurus
steps.text: Hmph. In my view...

steps.name: Ratatos
steps.text: I said keep it down, Sciurus. If you really have something to say, you can go outside, and then tell the mountains about it.

steps.name: Ratatos
steps.text: Of course, I won't let you back indoors.

steps.name: Sciurus
steps.text: Tch. Fine, I'll just shut up then.

steps.name: Sciurus
steps.text: (Murmured) So happy to talk to yourself.

steps.name: Devotee
steps.text: Sir Arctosz arrives.

At the summit of Karlan in winter, the frigid winds never rest, but the look in Arctosz's eyes, and the sound of his great axe as it drags along the ground in bursts, come to fool people—it's as if the winds are his to bring.

steps.name: Ratatos
steps.text: Look who's here, Arctosz, my fine friend.

steps.name: Arctosz
steps.text: Enciodes?

steps.name: Ratatos
steps.text: Who am I to answer that?

steps.name: Ratatos
steps.text: I thought you would've bumped into each other outside and settled everything there, and that way I wouldn't need to be tormented in here, and I could go home happy.

steps.name: Arctosz
steps.text: How surprising that something can even torment you, Ratatos.

steps.name: Ratatos
steps.text: Of course. I've got torment to the nines.

steps.name: Ratatos
steps.text: Such as, more and more people in my territory wanting to work for a living at Enciodes's instead.

steps.name: Ratatos
steps.text: Or, Gulo, the most able officer you have, not showing up today. Why?

steps.name: Arctosz
steps.text: He caught a cold.

steps.name: Ratatos
steps.text: Kjerag's sturdiest soldier catching a cold. That's no good omen.

steps.name: Ratatos
steps.text: Looks like we'll need that man under Enciodes to give him some treatment. Gnosis, that one.

steps.name: Arctosz
steps.text: He'll get better on his own.

steps.name: Ratatos
steps.text: Fine, fine. No good deed of mine goes unpunished.

steps.name: Ratatos
steps.text: Seeing as you're here, it looks like we're just missing Enciodes now.
The three o'clock chime has not yet sounded.

steps.name: Enciodes
steps.text: I see I've kept the two of you waiting.

steps.name: Devotee
steps.text: S-Sir Enciodes and the Great Elder arrive!

steps.name: Ratatos
steps.text: Hm?

steps.name: Ratatos
steps.text: Tch, there's a mystery. Why are the two of them together...?

steps.name: Ratatos
steps.text: Enciodes, don't tell me you went praying to the Saintess before coming to this meeting?

steps.name: Enciodes
steps.text: Far from it. I met the Great Elder along the way, and had a few words with him.

steps.name: Enciodes
steps.text: Great Elder, you first.

steps.name: Great Elder
steps.text: A fine courtesy.
The entrance to the hall slowly shuts, the air inside settling down in an instant after.
The Great Elder sits straight in the middle, Arctosz and Ratatos stand to one side, and Enciodes to the other.
The gulf of difference is stark.

steps.name: Great Elder
steps.text: Former Tri-Clan Councils always had us sit together, talking of the year's crop of affairs, of whose house had done more, and of whose required assistance after blights of snow.

steps.name: Great Elder
steps.text: I had not foreseen such a topic at today's council... *sigh*.

steps.name: Arctosz
steps.text: You'll want to really grill Enciodes about that.

steps.name: Enciodes
steps.text: No need for such aggression, Arctosz.

steps.name: Enciodes
steps.text: As the Great Elder said, the Tri-Clan Council should be no place for us to blame and reproach each other.

steps.name: Ratatos
steps.text: I wonder if you've heard one about the pot and the kettle, Enciodes.

steps.name: Great Elder
steps.text: Enough, enough. Given we are all here, we shall commence this meeting of the Tri-Clan Council.

steps.name: Great Elder
steps.text: By Kjeragandr.

steps.name: Everyone
steps.text: By Kjeragandr.

steps.name: Great Elder
steps.text: I presume all three are aware of the purpose of this Council.

steps.name: Great Elder
steps.text: On Mr. Arctosz and Ms. Ratatos's proposal, last meeting, that the Silverashes would cede governing authority over the valleys and mining regions, for the Paleroches and Browntails to then administrate.

steps.name: Great Elder
steps.text: In addition, the Silverashes' withdrawal from the parliament of the Tri-Clan Council.

steps.name: Enciodes
steps.text: Gnosis Edelweiss has been expelled from his post by myself. I believe both of you know this already.

steps.name: Arctosz
steps.text: What good does knowing that do? Gnosis is your aide. How could his actions not have been according to your instruction?

steps.name: Arctosz
steps.text: If you think pinning the blame on him will let you escape punishment, then think again!

steps.name: Enciodes
steps.text: Arctosz, why come to such an arbitrary conclusion?

steps.name: Arctosz
steps.text: Enciodes, there's much I can tolerate from you. You can open your factories in your territory, do your business, recruit your foreigners.

steps.name: Arctosz
steps.text: That is your territory. Whatever ghoulish form you twist it into, it's not my concern.

steps.name: Arctosz
steps.text: But never should you have led your railroad to Karlan, bringing the copper stench onto holy earth. And your mining up to Karlan's foot, extracting resources in secret, is beyond the pale.

steps.name: Arctosz
steps.text: What do you take the ground of Karlan for—what do you take the land of Kjeragandr for?

steps.name: Arctosz
steps.text: You even plotted against any inspection teams so that they wouldn't investigate your factories. My subordinates are still bedbound for it.

steps.name: Arctosz
steps.text: Is that what you want to say? That these are all the doing of that accursed Edelweiss, and nothing to do with you?!

steps.name: Enciodes
steps.text: Gnosis was once my most trusted partner, and I mistakenly gave him too much power.

steps.name: Enciodes
steps.text: For that, I am deeply regretful.

steps.name: Enciodes
steps.text: What of you, Ratatos? Is there really no leeway to reverse course between us?

steps.name: Ratatos
steps.text: *sigh* I really would love to help you, Enciodes.

steps.name: Ratatos
steps.text: After all, six whole years ago, it was me who paved your way back into this hall. Of course it hurts, pushing you out again by my own hands.

steps.name: Ratatos
steps.text: But in the end, when it's about all of Kjerag, I just can't defend you.

steps.name: Enciodes
steps.text: Though I believe the Browntails have benefited, greatly, from business in Turicum.

steps.name: Ratatos
steps.text: Am I denying that? It's not just money in our pockets, we can reap the rewards with our subjects too. Who wouldn't be a fan? Only sticks-in-the-mud like Arctosz.

steps.name: Ratatos
steps.text: But even though people talk behind my back thanks to it, crying witch about me, I still have a bottom line, Enciodes.

steps.name: Ratatos
steps.text: I don't know what you read or learned in those four years you studied outside, that drives you to abuse our trust to this point.

steps.name: Ratatos
steps.text: I was wrong about you six years ago, Enciodes. I'll pay for that in time—but you're going to pay first.

steps.name: Enciodes
steps.text: Ceding the valleys and mines under our jurisdiction, as well as the Silverashes' seat at the Tri-Clan Council. These are your demands. Is it not an excessively high price?

steps.name: Enciodes
steps.text: Karlan Trade has already stricken its then-director in these affairs, Gnosis, off its register. The company's growth policy has recently mildened too, that much is plain to see.

steps.name: Ratatos
steps.text: Too late, Enciodes.

steps.name: Ratatos
steps.text: If this price wasn't high, how would you ever remember it?

steps.name: Arctosz
steps.text: If you wanted to seek forgiveness, you never would've done any of this in the first place.

steps.name: Arctosz
steps.text: But since you have done it already, then today, here and now, you must pay something for it.

steps.name: Arctosz
steps.text: Are you handing over governance of the valleys and mines, or are you not? Are you seceding from the Tri-Clan Council, or are you not?

steps.name: Enciodes
steps.text: All I have done up to now was for the development of Kjerag.

steps.name: Enciodes
steps.text: That it would worsen our relations with the Paleroches and Browntails to this present extent, was never my wish.

steps.name: Enciodes
steps.text: And from the exchanges I've just had with the two of you, I see this worsening is already unavertable, and unredeemable.

steps.name: Enciodes
steps.text: I somewhat foresaw it, but to arrive at this moment in reality, at this time of grievance and ultimatum in this hall, still fills me with sorrow.

steps.name: Enciodes
steps.text: But I truly cannot bear to see a fissure arise in the three clans that govern Kjerag together.

steps.name: Enciodes
steps.text: Dissent in the three clans signifies dissent in Kjerag. It signifies, that Kjeragandr's people, are soon to lose their collective homeland.

steps.name: Arctosz
steps.text: Enciodes, if you truly thought so, if you truly ever thought so for even one moment...

steps.name: Arctosz
steps.text: You would have sent yourself packing from Kjerag, back to your Victoria, and been a worry less on Kjerag herself!

steps.name: Enciodes
steps.text: Arctosz. I, Enciodes Silverash, am the head of the Silverashes.

steps.name: Enciodes
steps.text: This means I must bear my responsibility for the future of Kjerag, and fulfil what is obliged of me.

steps.name: Enciodes
steps.text: I don't know what makes you feel I should have stayed in Victoria. Is it because those days of only two clans in parliament made you feel so much more powerful?

steps.name: Enciodes
steps.text: Not to mention, my reforms in the years I've led the Silverashes are a done reality...

steps.name: Enciodes
steps.text: The people of my territory haven't just gained from the way of life I've brought, they've continued to advance such lives by their own accord.

steps.name: Enciodes
steps.text: Even if I leave, the machines will still work, and the trains on the tracks will still set into motion.

steps.name: Enciodes
steps.text: Or do you truly believe that if I hand off the valleys and mines today, and cease operation of those factories and railroads...

steps.name: Enciodes
steps.text: That the people working there, the people benefiting from what it produces, will accede?

steps.name: Ratatos
steps.text: That's your problem to solve, Enciodes.

steps.name: Enciodes
steps.text: No, Ratatos. Maybe you have incredible trust in my problem-solving ability, but at base, this is not a problem I alone must face.

steps.name: Enciodes
steps.text: You wouldn't suggest that the Browntails' subjects have never profited any from these years Karlan Trade has done business?

steps.name: Enciodes
steps.text: How many people have the Originium stoves kept going through the coldest winters, procured from Columbia by Karlan Trade? There are no Catastrophes in our mountains, but the ice and snow still claim lives.

steps.name: Enciodes
steps.text: What is so disgraceful about the herders' prods, or the fertilizer that comes from Victoria?

steps.name: Ratatos
steps.text: You brought about this situation today—including your constant embellishment of yourself—and now you're using that same situation to menace us, shamelessly.

steps.name: Ratatos
steps.text: Get it out. Say this is all your accomplishment. Say you're powerless to give those of Kjerag self-sufficiency, and that you're not afraid to have them mocking you. You, head of the Silverashes.

steps.name: Enciodes
steps.text: Wrong, Ratatos.

steps.name: Enciodes
steps.text: To menace is the bluff of one who lacks confidence, while I—am only recounting the truth.

steps.name: Enciodes
steps.text: You deem Karlan Trade as a menace to Kjerag. That, in itself, is a mockery beyond the heavens.

steps.name: Ratatos
steps.text: Keh...

steps.name: Ratatos
steps.text: You've got some gall by the sound of it, Enciodes. I remember. You've been good at talking this sort of talk ever since you were young.

steps.name: Arctosz
steps.text: Don't waste your breath, Enciodes.

steps.name: Arctosz
steps.text: Today, you will...

steps.name: Enciodes
steps.text: Would I not hand it over today, General Gulo would have directly 'assumed' control of the valleys, having been stationed close by long ago.

steps.name: Arctosz
steps.text: You...

steps.name: Enciodes
steps.text: Don't be so quick to resort to force, Arctosz.

steps.name: Enciodes
steps.text: I can make commitments and decisions, accordingly, to your proposals.

steps.name: Enciodes
steps.text: Conflict has been far from my intent up to now. As the head, I will not put up with any losses either.

steps.name: Enciodes
steps.text: But if it's for putting this grievous state of affairs in check, for the alliance of the three clans of the snow mountains, then in the capacity of Kjeragandr's people, the Silverashes can make concessions.

steps.name: Enciodes
steps.text: —I am fully able to offer the valleys and mines, with both hands.

steps.name: Ratatos
steps.text: You're serious?

steps.name: Arctosz
steps.text: You can say a fine line! Enciodes, there's no one here who'll be taken in by your drivel!

steps.name: Enciodes
steps.text: Hence why I say, Arctosz, don't rush.

steps.name: Enciodes
steps.text: Impetuousness will be your weakness, guardian axe of Kjeragandr, most pious soldier of Kjerag.

steps.name: Enciodes
steps.text: I can accept these conditions you two have devised. But it will not be handed to the Paleroches, nor the Browntails.

steps.name: Arctosz
steps.text: Then to whom do you give it? What, Kjeragandr?!

steps.name: Enciodes
steps.text: Completely correct, Arctosz, most faithful of the people of Kjeragandr.

steps.name: Enciodes
steps.text: Every inch of territory of the Silverashes, and of you all too, is fundamentally accorded to us by Kjeragandr's trust. We merely supervise it in Kjeragandr's place.

steps.name: Ratatos
steps.text: ...Hold on, you can't be...

steps.name: Enciodes
steps.text: It is as you imagine, Ratatos.

steps.name: Enciodes
steps.text: I've decided I will hear your demands, and give the Silverashes' valleys and mines in whole to the Vine-Bead Court, for the Saintess to handle its factories and pits.

steps.name: Arctosz
steps.text: What?!

steps.name: Enciodes
steps.text: So as to avert conflict between the three clans, Kjerag ought to have a leader who can hold the faith of both the three clans, and the Snow Realm's citizens, at once.

steps.name: Enciodes
steps.text: Though we've managed, I believe that having the vicar of Kjeragandr take control of Kjerag once again, as in times past, is a fair and reasonable thing.

steps.name: Enciodes
steps.text: I imagine that peacefully settling this issue, peacefully partitioning the Silverashes' assets, and peacefully avoiding a direct clash of the three families, is what we hope for by all rights.

steps.name: Enciodes
steps.text: Ratatos, Arctosz—I can give up my valley and mines on this one condition. What do you think?
A spell of silence. The attending nobles look amongst each other, trying to comprehend what purpose lies within the words.
The only sound, the scratching of the transcriber's pen, but that freezes too a few short seconds later, hung in the atmosphere.
The first to break the silence is a pencil as it carelessly clatters to the ground, alongside a stunned gasp from an unknown someone.
Immediately, consciously, low murmurs of discussion arise one after another, as if a pan of rösti in lowly heated oil.

steps.name: Talkative Noblewoman
steps.text: Look! Is that the man from the Edelweisses...

steps.name: Scathing Nobleman
steps.text: That Gnosis cur has the nerve to show his face here. I spit on him.

steps.name: Talkative Noblewoman
steps.text: Good word, he's turned this way!

steps.name: Scathing Nobleman
steps.text: Pah. See the look in his eyes. Heaven knows why Mr. Enciodes ever gave him such great responsibility, when his parents clearly plotted...

steps.name: Talkative Noblewoman
steps.text: Tut-tut-tut, shush it, now! You'll anger Kjeragandr if you speak of these things atop Karlan!

steps.name: Talkative Noblewoman
steps.text: Though you have to admit, his happy days are at an end. Mr. Enciodes obviously couldn't tolerate his conduct one second longer.

steps.name: Scathing Nobleman
steps.text: Really? Did Mr. Enciodes finally pull him from his post?

steps.name: Talkative Noblewoman
steps.text: Yes! Didn't you know? At the Council last month, he removed him from his office on the spot...

steps.name: Scathing Nobleman
steps.text: He's already out, then? That's wonderful! His number was long up!

steps.name: Monch
steps.text: Sir Gnosis.

steps.name: Gnosis
steps.text: I've warned that we should not converse on these occasions.

steps.name: Monch
steps.text: Yes, my apologies.

steps.name: Monch
steps.text: Only... I received an urgent message. The train carrying Rhodes Island's delegation is almost at Karlan's foot already.

steps.name: Monch
steps.text: You had some interest in this company. Do you want to go and meet them?

steps.name: Gnosis
steps.text: The Snow Realm has reached a major juncture. If they're external forces that have been drawn in, then I'll naturally meet them when the time comes. No need to go out of my way.

steps.name: Gnosis
steps.text: Besides... I'm merely an employee on probation now. What position do I have as pretext to meet them?

steps.name: Monch
steps.text: It really was disappointing to see how Enciodes acted, ejecting you as a figurehead just to appease the other two clans.

steps.name: Gnosis
steps.text: Appease? Enciodes's thoughts are by no means as simple as that.

steps.name: Gnosis
steps.text: I've heard Rhodes Island really did succeed in slowing the exacerbation of Ensia's Oripathy?

steps.name: Monch
steps.text: Yes...

steps.name: Gnosis
steps.text: Hm. Then they do, in fact, have the resources to win the Silverashes' favor.

steps.name: Gnosis
steps.text: But the attention of Enciodes is both a blessing and curse. No easy judgments yet.

steps.name: Monch
steps.text: You mean...

steps.name: Gnosis
steps.text: There is no extraneous meaning to what I said.

steps.name: Gnosis
steps.text: Anyhow, presumably those in the company must have applauded and cheered, the same way those two dilettantes did just now, hearing I was gone.

steps.name: Monch
steps.text: None of them understand your worth, Sir Gnosis.

steps.name: Gnosis
steps.text: Using the word 'worth' to describe a person implies that person can be weighed.

steps.name: Monch
steps.text: Sir...

steps.name: Gnosis
steps.text: By now, Enciodes should have proposed his idea for the Saintess to lead the Tri-Clan Council.

steps.name: Gnosis
steps.text: The meeting hall, at this moment, should be utter chaos.

steps.name: Gnosis
steps.text: Enciodes, in the end, this is the step you took after all.

steps.name: Monch
steps.text: You're the one who understands Enciodes the most. Only you can stand in the way of his ambitions.

steps.name: Gnosis
steps.text: The wind's picked up. It's going to snow.
A massive snowflake sticks against Gnosis's shoulder, only for the frigid wind to pitilessly, immediately blow it off.
Kjerag's snowstorms are far from rare. They only need the clouds to gather thick enough, waiting just for a turning point.
And once the equilibrium of the air that supported those clouds is smashed, and loses its bracing power—

a.text: Does Enciodes seriously mean for the Saintess to become Kjerag's queen?
Impossible! This is Enciodes we're talking about!
But he seemed serious about those ideas he spouted just now...
No matter how you put it, think how incredible it'd be if Kjerag could unite under the Saintess's leadership! Kjeragandr's land really should return to Kjeragandr!

steps.text: The whispers amongst the bystanders come together, and momentarily, the roar of the wind outside the window is covered by the voices.

steps.name: Ratatos
steps.text: ...Enciodes, do you have any idea what you're saying?

steps.name: Enciodes
steps.text: I'm clear as could be.

steps.name: Enciodes
steps.text: Let us lay everything out in the open.

steps.name: Enciodes
steps.text: I originally held that, so long as results were had and the Silverashes' sincerity was clear to you all, you would discard your prejudices, and hand in hand with me, lead Kjerag forward.

steps.name: Enciodes
steps.text: If the three clans could act together, then regardless of any difference in earnings—

steps.name: Enciodes
steps.text: A country's stance upon foreign trade versus a company's stance upon foreign trade are completely divorced concepts, and the results obtained will be a world apart.

steps.name: Enciodes
steps.text: Maybe my pace was too fast, and led you to believe instead I was planning to submissively hand Kjerag to outsiders?

steps.name: Arctosz
steps.text: As if you weren't? Enciodes, Karlan IS NOT your theater to act in! Kjeragandr will punish you for every lie you've spewed!

steps.name: Enciodes
steps.text: In that case, that Karlan still permits me to stand here is my greatest proof.

steps.name: Enciodes
steps.text: Leave it at that. I know full well I can't change your thinking, but I don't plan to alter Karlan Trade policy because of your shortsightedness either.

steps.name: Enciodes
steps.text: Karlan Trade values Kjerag's mines and factories, but they aren't the totality of the company. Letting them bring the company into stasis is far less worth it to me.

steps.name: Enciodes
steps.text: If we let an eye for an eye go any further, then in the long run, we'll have spent excessive energy on uniting our views, and it'll have given outside threats a chance to hijack.

steps.name: Enciodes
steps.text: Like you, this is in no way what I want.

steps.name: Enciodes
steps.text: Therefore—

steps.name: Enciodes
steps.text: I ultimately resolve to hand over all executive power to the Saintess.

steps.name: Enciodes
steps.text: It will be for the Saintess to determine. I can accept this arrangement, and I believe all present can too.

steps.name: Arctosz
steps.text: A heap of nonsense!

steps.name: Arctosz
steps.text: Who would believe words like these from someone trampling on the faith of Kjeragandr?!

steps.name: Enciodes
steps.text: Trampling?

steps.name: Enciodes
steps.text: I know that's how you see it. Many harbor prejudice towards the change Karlan Trade has brought.

steps.name: Enciodes
steps.text: But labor is the very foundation on which Kjerag was stood.

steps.name: Enciodes
steps.text: Forget not that should they still have work at noon, the Browntails' people pass on kneeling in prayer to Karlan.

steps.name: Enciodes
steps.text: And if things are busy, they certainly do not take the monthly visit to Karlan to hear the teachings.

steps.name: Ratatos
steps.text: Ha. Enciodes, pulling some hamfisted strawman like this isn't one bit persuasive.

steps.name: Ratatos
steps.text: What next? Are you going to say that everything you've done to Karlan is by Kjeragandr's counsel?

steps.name: Enciodes
steps.text: 'Kjeragandr,' Page 1, Line 1.

steps.name: Enciodes
steps.text: 'Her tears are the ice eternally unmelting, Her back the unbreaking mountain, Her breath the cold wind of winter, Her smile the warm light of spring.'

steps.name: Enciodes
steps.text: 'When She awakes, shall the mountains summon Her, and the sky cast down lustrous spectra.'

steps.name: Enciodes
steps.text: No one has ever said that the Holy Mount can truly stand for Her.

steps.name: Enciodes
steps.text: Mt. Karlan's uniqueness is owed to the Vine-Bead Court being situated on it.

steps.name: Enciodes
steps.text: If you denounce me for harm of the Vine-Bead Court's interests, I will readily concede that. Besides, I have brought my full good faith.

steps.name: Enciodes
steps.text: And in addition, 'those who toil will hold power, and those who idle will suffer.'

steps.name: Enciodes
steps.text: I have never gone against Her teachings.

steps.name: Arctosz
steps.text: Utter, utter tripe!

steps.name: Arctosz
steps.text: The Vine-Bead Court is Kjeragandr's representative upon this land, and the Saintess of the Vine-Bead Court Her Terran speaker! How do you think you can change this with a mere few utterances?!

steps.name: Arctosz
steps.text: Great Elder, will the Vine-Bead Court suffer these wild lies?!

steps.name: Great Elder
steps.text: Naturally, I have to protest what Mr. Enciodes says.

steps.name: Great Elder
steps.text: However, day in and day out, the scholars wage countless disputes over interpretations of Her words. The Vine-Bead Court is not a place of outlawed dissent, by any means.

steps.name: Enciodes
steps.text: Who is right, and who is wrong? Far be it from you or me to have the final say, Arctosz.

steps.name: Enciodes
steps.text: Page 3, Line 5.

steps.name: Enciodes
steps.text: 'In the beginning, Kjerag had but one untamed settlement, so until She lifted Her head from amidst the mountains.'
This time, following Enciodes's start, some nobles present notably begin to recite alongside him.
'She became as human, and lived in survival with the untamed. Yet they feared Her might, and honored Her as Divine.'
'More came to gather at Her side, and so was Kjerag born, and She, its first ruler.'
'Under Her guidance, did Kjerag flourish and thrive in bountifulness.'

steps.name: Enciodes
steps.text: Arctosz, tell me. What does Page 321, Line 1 say?

steps.name: Arctosz
steps.text: '...After She held the kingdom for three centuries, there came one sudden day when She passed the ruler's title to Her helper, and vanished amidst the blizzard.'

steps.name: Ratatos
steps.text: 'Henceforth, Kjerag was given unto the people's hands.'

steps.name: Enciodes
steps.text: Everyone, we are all of Kjerag, and all Her people.

steps.name: Enciodes
steps.text: It is exactly as I said before—

steps.name: Enciodes
steps.text: If there is someone able to determine how we should proceed, then it is not I, nor you, nor Ratatos.

steps.name: Enciodes
steps.text: This someone must be Her speaker, the Saintess.

steps.name: Enciodes
steps.text: That we do not trust each other won't matter.

steps.name: Enciodes
steps.text: The Saintess will determine for us, and show us towards the future.

steps.name: Enciodes
steps.text: Or do you mean to admit, somehow, that you don't trust the Saintess to make the fairest ruling, that you don't trust Her speaker upon the land?
In an instant, the attention of every noble there focuses onto Arctosz.

steps.name: Arctosz
steps.text: You...! Enciodes, how dare you!

steps.name: Ratatos
steps.text: Enciodes, if you're hoping this level of provocation will rouse any reaction in us, then that's far too disappointing of you.

steps.name: Ratatos
steps.text: The Saintess was born a Silverash, that we all know.

steps.name: Ratatos
steps.text: But her character is equivalently common knowledge.

steps.name: Ratatos
steps.text: She is still Kjerag's Saintess. From the moment she received the glory and duty of Kjeragandr, the people of Kjerag have been witness to her every word and action.

steps.name: Ratatos
steps.text: Her conduct has been impartial, ever since she took up the title. As things stand, how can we be skeptical of her simply for her common birth?

steps.name: Ratatos
steps.text: It's like you just said. Kjeragandr was broad of heart, and resolved to give Kjerag's future to Her people.

steps.name: Ratatos
steps.text: But you. You, Enciodes, choosing only now after all this time to bring up Kjeragandr, expounding on Her virtue and benevolence. Is that not out of some ulterior motive, really?

steps.name: Ratatos
steps.text: You are the one disrespecting the Saintess, Enciodes, coming in with sophistry to coerce and take advantage of her people!

steps.name: Enciodes
steps.text: That's a grave accusation, Ratatos, far graver than your criticisms of Karlan Trade.

steps.name: Enciodes
steps.text: It seems our continuing this discussion further will only add to the maelstrom of conjecture. Given so, we may as well ask the Saintess to come here, and we'll set things straight in front of her.

steps.name: Arctosz
steps.text: Hmph, no objections. With all three clans gathered here, I expect there won't be any room for your tricks.

steps.name: Enciodes
steps.text: Well, then. In the interest of fairness, may we trouble the Great Elder in our humble request of the Saintess?

steps.name: Great Elder
steps.text: So be it. I'll go and ask her. Exercise patience, please.

steps.name: Enya
steps.text: I think it might be snowing outside.

steps.name: Kjarr
steps.text: What's so strange about that? The snow never stops falling on this mountain.

steps.name: Enya
steps.text: Something's different.

steps.name: Enya
steps.text: ...So, Enciodes proposes the three families hand their power to me, for me to decide Kjerag's future?

steps.name: Kjarr
steps.text: Indeed.

steps.name: Kjarr
steps.text: What do you think of it, Enya?

steps.name: Kjarr
steps.text: Well met, Great Elder.

steps.name: Great Elder
steps.text: Enya. Here you are.

steps.name: Great Elder
steps.text: I imagine you've probably heard about the assembly's affairs.

steps.name: Enya
steps.text: If you mean the transferral of power, yes, I already know.

steps.name: Enya
steps.text: There's been progress, then, if you've come for me now?

steps.name: Great Elder
steps.text: Keen ever since you were little, young one.

steps.name: Great Elder
steps.text: It's reached the point where the clans' views clash like fire and water.

steps.name: Great Elder
steps.text: Before this Council convened, Silverash gave me a hint or two... that under the current situation, the plan he'd suggest may well deescalate.

steps.name: Enya
steps.text: It seems you don't approve of my actions last Council after all, Great Elder.

steps.name: Great Elder
steps.text: Enya, oh, Enya.

steps.name: Great Elder
steps.text: Come... child, look outside. Could you know the years it took, for the frost and snow to finally cover these mountains?

steps.name: Great Elder
steps.text: And could you know, how many years had to pass, for us to have this pure and holy summit where we stand?

steps.name: Enya
steps.text: ...I understand.

steps.name: Enya
steps.text: But—'Her tears are the ice eternally unmelting, Her back the unbreaking mountain, Her breath the cold wind of winter, Her smile the warm light of spring.'

steps.name: Enya
steps.text: If everything was Kjeragandr's gift, then why must Kjeragandr's people still fear the blizzard?

steps.name: Great Elder
steps.text: ...In that respect, you and him do seem alike... yet different, too...

steps.name: Enya
steps.text: Um, pardon me...?

steps.name: Great Elder
steps.text: Nothing, just an old man thinking aloud.

steps.name: Great Elder
steps.text: What you say is correct, Saintess.

steps.name: Great Elder
steps.text: You've spent all your time atop this summit, and the mountains have bowed to Kjeragandr's speaker in turn. To think so is quite right.

steps.name: Great Elder
steps.text: However, in snow this great, built up over so many years, how many of Kjeragandr's people would be buried, should it ever collapse?

steps.name: Great Elder
steps.text: To me, Kjerag's peace of mind has always come first and foremost.

steps.name: Great Elder
steps.text: I trust, Saintess, that you are the same.

steps.name: Great Elder
steps.text: Hum... it's about time.

steps.name: Great Elder
steps.text: The three are still in the hall awaiting you. You cannot appear too soon, but I wouldn't advise you be too late either. Now is the perfect time.

steps.name: Kjarr
steps.text: May you both come this way, please.

steps.name: Enya
steps.text: Alright.

steps.name: Enya
steps.text: Kjerag's peace of mind...

steps.name: Enya
steps.text: Letting this snow carry on building underfoot, without a place for us to clear a way... will that be peace for Kjerag?

steps.name: Enya
steps.text: Kjeragandr, I pray, watch over your people...
In the wake of the blizzard sweeping the mountain, the clear, sharp bell strokes come as if from the heavens to the ears of Kjeragandr's people.
Where she passes, no noble fails to stand, offering the most formal etiquette, chanting the most devout prayer.
'Frost and snow have fallen by your will, to bring to Kjerag blessings.'

steps.name: Enciodes
steps.text: Saintess, it's been long.

steps.name: Enya
steps.text: With your litany of occupations, you've neglected worship, Sir Enciodes. It truly has been long.

steps.name: Enciodes
steps.text: You requested an investigation of the valleys and mines prior, Saintess. I could not, of course, neglect that.

steps.name: Enciodes
steps.text: Once all this is settled and done with, I will personally lead a procession in worship to Karlan.

steps.name: Enya
steps.text: Your faith in Kjeragandr is apparent throughout. Why be so elaborate in proving it?

steps.name: Enciodes
steps.text: That's a fine jest, Great Saintess.

steps.name: Enya
steps.text: I hear a sister of yours has come back to Kjerag.

steps.name: Enciodes
steps.text: You're well-informed, Saintess. She should be on the path to Karlan with an honored guest at this very moment.

steps.name: Enya
steps.text: A guest?

steps.name: Enciodes
steps.text: Indeed. Up till now, my sister has been receiving treatment at a medical firm called Rhodes Island, for her Oripathy.

steps.name: Enciodes
steps.text: For the coming Grand Ceremony, I've invited one of said firm's leaders to visit Kjerag, as a gesture of thanks.

steps.name: Enya
steps.text: You care much for your sister, Sir Enciodes. Truly, it is admirable.

steps.name: Enciodes
steps.text: ...You flatter me, Saintess.

steps.name: Enciodes
steps.text: I presume you already know of my proposal. What do you think of it?

steps.name: Enya
steps.text: What are Sir Arctosz and Lady Ratatos's considerations?

steps.name: Arctosz
steps.text: I, Arctosz, with my faith in Kjeragandr visible to all, say that let alone merely having the Saintess be the mediator of the three clans—

steps.name: Ratatos
steps.text: Hold it, Arctosz!

steps.name: Arctosz
steps.text: —I could hand my position as head to her, and what shame would it be?

steps.name: Enya
steps.text: And you, Lady Ratatos?
Who could possibly say no in this moment?
Who would dare say no in this moment?

steps.name: Ratatos
steps.text: For the Great Saintess to be the arbitrator of the three clans, in this present situation, is indeed the best option.

steps.name: Enya
steps.text: I understand.

steps.name: Enya
steps.text: As the three clans' heads all submit to this, and are willing to entrust themselves to me...

steps.name: Enya
steps.text: I shall—

steps.name: Enya
steps.text: Respond in kind to all, and assume the duty of guiding Kjerag.
